newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas jumps late, Sept hits new high.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas jumps late, Sept hits new high.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures extended gains late Monday in active trade, with firmer cash prices and technical buying after Friday's breakout driving spot-September to a new contract high, market sources said.

At 1415 EDT, September was up 11.1 cents at $2.35 per million British thermal units after rallying to a new high of $2.385 by early afternoon. October was 11 cents higher at $2.355. Most others were up by 1.5 to 10.5 cents.
"Technically, we closed above the trendline Friday, so we're seeing some additional trade and fund buying today," said one Midwest futures trader.
While storage concerns and heat in the Southwest should keep the bears at bay near-term, some said cash, for the first time in many weeks, now lags the screen by almost 10 cents.

"In one day, we (cash) went from a nickel over (futures) to more than a nickel under," said one East Coast trader, noting East Coast weather looked pretty cool this week though Texas was still fairly hot.
Forecasters expect below-normal Midwest and Northeast temperatures for most of the week, with a slight warming trend by the weekend.

But chart traders agreed September's close Friday above key resistance along the down trendline turned the technical picture bullish and most expected more upside near-term. Resistance was now seen at the new contract high of $2.385, with further selling likely at the May 7 spot continuation high of $2.43. Support was now pegged at $2.20, then at $2.15-2.16 and along the short-term up trendline in the $2.12 area. Key support was expected at the prominent $2.045 low.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices firmed one or two cents to the $2.20 area or better, with gas at the Hub pegged in the mid-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the mid-teens. Forecasts for milder New York weather this week pressured city gate prices down slightly to the low-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 41,576 contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On the KCBT, September jumped 10.4 cents to $2.22, while deferreds were steady to 13.6 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.7 cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
